docRequirement: hooks-guide.md:973 (§ *Stop hook hits the block cap*): "If your hook legitimately needs more than eight iterations to converge, raise the cap with [`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`](/docs/en/env-vars)." The linked page gives the full semantics — env-vars.md:336: "Maximum number of consecutive times a Stop or SubagentStop hook may block the turn from ending before Claude Code overrides it and ends the turn anyway (default: 8). Set to `0` to disable the cap." So the binding is a three-part knob: an environment variable named `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`, defaulting to 8, scoped to `Stop` and `SubagentStop`, with `0` meaning no cap.
current:
The cap is a private module constant with no override of any kind. `const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS = 8;` at packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:136, read at exactly one site: packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:564 `if (streak > MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS)`, which logs `this.debug(...)` at :565 and returns without queueing the block's `reason`. The streak it counts lives in the in-memory per-agent map at packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:338 and is incremented at :562-563, reset on any non-blocking result at :558-560.

The mechanism is live on BOTH documented events, contrary to how the filed verdict reads it: `Stop` via packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7312 (`.then(result => this.recordHookBlockFeedback('Stop', result))`), and `SubagentStop` via packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5814 (`managed.agent?.recordHookBlockFeedback(event, result)`, where `event` is narrowed to `'SubagentStop'` by the early return at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5757). A third, undocumented-by-Claude event — `ConfigChange` — shares the same counter at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7340. The same streak also sources the `stop_hook_active` hook-input field at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7300 and, for the child path, at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5777-5779 through `stopHookActive` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7284, contract at packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:895).

Absence re-checked with `grep -a` per the NUL-byte trap: `grep -ran "hookBlockCap|blockCap|STOP_HOOK" packages apps/electron/src apps/cli/src docs-site` → 0 hits; `grep -ran "MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS" packages apps` returns only base-agent.ts and the build outputs apps/electron/dist/main.cjs:398302/398543. The fork does honour numeric Claude env knobs elsewhere, with an established shape: packages/shared/src/config/print-background-wait.ts:41-89 exports a Nessy name (`NESSY_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`), the Claude spelling as a compat alias (`CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`, :44), a default constant (:53), a documented `0` sentinel (:56), and `resolvePrintBackgroundWaitCeilingMs(env = process.env)` (:77-89) that falls back to the default on a malformed value. packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:9-12 records the same Claude→Nessy naming convention. Nothing equivalent exists for this cap.
divergence: Only the escape hatch is missing; the capped behaviour itself matches. Specifically: (1) neither `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` nor a `NESSY_`-spelled equivalent is read anywhere, so the cap cannot be raised; (2) the documented `0` = "disable the cap" state is unreachable — with a hardcoded 8, `streak > 8` always eventually trips; (3) the value 8 and the event scope (`Stop`, `SubagentStop`) are both correct, and the comparison `streak > cap` honours exactly 8 consecutive blocks and suppresses the 9th, which is what env-vars.md:336's "maximum number of consecutive times a … hook may block … before Claude Code overrides it" specifies and what packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/hook-block-decisions.test.ts:179-189 already pins. So this is a pure add-a-resolver gap, not a wrong value and not a wrong boundary.

change.what: New module, copied in shape from packages/shared/src/config/print-background-wait.ts:38-89. Header quotes env-vars.md:336 verbatim. Exports: `STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP_ENV_VAR = 'NESSY_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP'`; `STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP_COMPAT_ENV_VAR = 'CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP'`; `DEFAULT_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP = 8`; `STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP_DISABLED = 0`; and `resolveStopHookBlockCap(env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env): number`. Resolution order and parsing must match the precedent exactly: the Nessy name wins when both are set (`env[NESSY] !== undefined ? env[NESSY] : env[COMPAT]`); `undefined` → 8; trim, then accept only `/^\d+$/`; reject non-safe-integers; any malformed value falls back to 8 (a typo must not silently buy an uncapped loop); `0` is returned verbatim and means "no cap".

Two lines of behaviour change. Delete the private constant at :136 and import `DEFAULT_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` + `resolveStopHookBlockCap` from '../config/stop-hook-block-cap.ts'. Inside `recordHookBlockFeedback`, after the streak increment at :562-563, add `const cap = event === 'Stop' || event === 'SubagentStop' ? resolveStopHookBlockCap() : DEFAULT_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP;` — the env knob is scoped to the two events env-vars.md:336 names, so `ConfigChange` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7340) keeps the fixed 8 rather than inheriting a knob no doc grants it. Change :564 to `if (cap !== 0 && streak > cap)`. Do NOT touch the `>` — see divergence (3). Update the debug string at :565 to print the effective cap instead of the literal "8-block override", and refresh the doc comments at :131-136 and :550-553 to cite env-vars.md:336 and name the `0` sentinel.

blastRadius:
Narrow, and it does NOT cross a persistence or wire boundary. The cap constant has exactly one reader (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:564); the streak it gates is an in-memory `Map` on the agent instance (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:338), never serialized to a session file, never sent over the RPC wire, never written to settings — so no schema or migration is involved and the repo's risk triggers do not fire.

What reads the surrounding mechanism: `recordHookBlockFeedback` has three production callers — packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7312 (`Stop`), packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7340 (`ConfigChange`), packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5814 (`SubagentStop`) — plus the backend contract declaration at packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:881. The queued reasons are drained once per turn by `consumeHookBlockFeedback` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:600-605) onto the next turn's user-message tail.

One adjacent surface the change must NOT disturb: the same streak feeds the `stop_hook_active` field delivered into user hook scripts' JSON stdin (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7300 and packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5777-5779 via `stopHookActive`, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7284, contract packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:895). That IS a boundary imported Claude/Codex plugin hooks read. Because the fix only changes the suppression threshold and never the counting, `stop_hook_active` semantics are untouched — including under `cap=0`, where the streak keeps growing and the field stays `true`.

Tests that must stay green: packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/hook-block-decisions.test.ts:173-209, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-lifecycle-hooks.test.ts:462-473, packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/subagent-stop-parent-scope.test.ts:201-236. Note two of those construct real `PiAgent`s, so an env var set in one test leaks into the next unless restored.

Env delivery is already solved on every shipped surface: a Finder-launched macOS build hydrates `process.env` from the user's login shell (apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:28-77) and skips only `VITE_*` (:17-19), so both spellings arrive; `nessy-server` and the CLI inherit the shell directly. No forwarding into the Pi subprocess is needed — `recordHookBlockFeedback` runs host-side. apps/electron/dist/main.cjs:398302 and apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js are build outputs; they regenerate and must not be hand-edited.
userImpact:
None observable for anyone on the default. The cap is 8 in both products, so behaviour is identical unless a user deliberately reaches for the documented knob.

It surfaces the moment someone follows hooks-guide.md § *Stop hook hits the block cap* — which is exactly the audience that hits it, since the doc prescribes the variable as the remedy for a hook that legitimately needs more than eight iterations. That user exports `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP=20`, restarts Nessy, and nothing changes: from the 9th consecutive block onward their Stop (or SubagentStop) hook's `reason` silently stops reaching the model, so the agent stops being told what still needs doing and the convergence loop the hook was driving stalls one iteration short. There is no UI signal at all — the suppression writes only `this.debug(...)` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:565), which lands in logs, not in the chat surface, so the symptom the user sees is "my hook stopped having any effect" with no explanation. `0` (disable the cap) is equally inert.

Note the fork's cap suppresses re-delivery of the reason rather than force-ending a continued turn (deliberate — packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:550-553; we cannot re-run a finished turn), so the symptom differs in shape from Claude's "turn ends with a warning", but the trigger point and the missing knob are the same.
notes:
Every file cited was read in full at the cited lines: base-agent.ts (118-147, 540-614), pi-agent.ts (7250-7349), SessionManager.ts (5740-5829), backend/types.ts (862-901), hook-block-decisions.test.ts (160-210), print-background-wait.ts (whole), background-task-settings.ts (1-123), shell-env.ts (1-90), plus both doc pages fetched with `curl -sL` (hooks-guide.md:958-973, env-vars.md:336).

Two corrections to the surviving verdict's own refinements, because both would misdirect the fix:

(a) The verdict says "no `SubagentStop` caller was found, so that half of the documented knob has no counterpart counter to configure at all." That is wrong. packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5814 calls `managed.agent?.recordHookBlockFeedback(event, result)` inside `executePiChildTerminalAutomation`, whose early return at :5757 (`if (event !== 'SubagentStop') return`) makes `event` exactly `'SubagentStop'`. Both documented events already share the one counter, so the fix is purely the resolver — nothing has to be built for SubagentStop.

(b) The verdict calls `streak > MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS` an off-by-one and says "an env override would also need the comparison fixed". I read it as correct: env-vars.md:336 defines the value as the "[m]aximum number of consecutive times a Stop or SubagentStop hook **may** block … **before** Claude Code overrides it", i.e. 8 blocks are honoured and the 9th is overridden — which is what `>` does and what hook-block-decisions.test.ts:179-189 already asserts (block 8 delivered, block 9 not). Changing it to `>=` would silently narrow the honoured count to 7 and break that test. This reading of the doc sentence is the one inference in this spec that is not code-verifiable; the rest is direct observation.

One scoping decision the implementer should be aware of rather than re-derive: the change list scopes the env-derived cap to `Stop`/`SubagentStop` and leaves `ConfigChange` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7340) on the fixed 8, because env-vars.md:336 names only those two events and our ConfigChange block is advisory (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7332-7338). Applying the knob uniformly to all three would also be defensible and is one fewer condition; it is a judgement call, not a correctness question.

Adjacent, out of scope for this sentence but worth a separate row if anyone sweeps hooks-guide again: when the cap trips, Claude "ends the turn with a warning" (hooks-guide.md:960) while we emit only a debug line (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:565) with nothing user-visible.
